title: fix(plugin-sharing)!: the ownership-queue service refuses a failed member read when the caller asks, and the approver slate and the sharing-recipient grant recompute ask

_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgTHYrCvGEffG5116eJa3f7Z)_

domain:server#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZMkHvuDeVYgTD73qF

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 队列服务的 `expandMembers` / `isMember` 在调用方传 `onFailedRead: 'refuse'` 时，队列背后任何一次读取失败（`sys_queue`、`sys_queue_member`、team、position、`sys_member`、BU 表）都抛错并点名那次读取，不再答「无人」。审批节点的 queue 审批人（D6）和共享规则的 queue 收件人重算（D7）都传 `'refuse'`；准入类（D3 访问、D4 认领、D5 分配池）不传，仍答「无人」。
- **为什么改：** ADR-0142 D2 修订：空展开是事实，读取失败是故障。以前成员表一故障，D7 就把这些成员的授权全撤了，D6 节点照样开给剩下的人、fallback、管理员或自动通过。第 1 部分（#30288）留下的 "Not yet" 在这里兑现。
- **风险与回滚：** 只有读取失败时多一次拒绝：D6 节点报可重试的 `APPROVER_DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE`；D7 各重算保留规则已有授权并告警，读取恢复后下一次重算收敛（有 pin）。默认 `'nobody'` 路径不变，激活台账读失败仍按「开启」。回滚即撤 PR。
- **先看：** `ownership-queue-service.ts` 的 `queueReadRefusal`、`specsReachUser`、`holderCheck` 与 `expandSpec` 的 `pass.refuse` 分支；`sharing-rule-service.ts`、`approval-service.ts` 各一处传参。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/ownership-queue.test.ts src/queue-recipient.test.ts -t "onFailedRead 'refuse'|keeps the queue-recipient|29604\] control"`，预期 13 条全过；`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run src/approval-service.test.ts -t "asks the queue service to refuse"`，预期 4 条全过。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位合同审查后落地。spec 文档措辞有 3 处 follow-up owed（见 Acceptance notes），本 PR 不改 spec。

Fixes #29604

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — `expandMembers` and `isMember` of the registered ownership-queue service, called with `onFailedRead: 'refuse'`, now reject when a read behind the queue fails, where they answered nobody. The approver slate asks for that answer, so an approval node whose `queue` approver cannot be read refuses to open under every `onEmptyApprovers` policy, where it opened on the rest of the slate, on the fallback slate or on the administrators, or auto-approved. The sharing-rule recompute asks for it too, so a whole-rule pass (`evaluateRule`, the REST evaluate endpoint, the boot backfill), the recipient-axis revoke and the per-user pass on a `queue`-recipient rule reject on such a failure, where they completed by revoking the grants of the members who could not be read. Every call without the option, and every read that succeeds, answers as before.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` corrected: it still said a `team` or `position` entry whose holder read failed keeps its literal slot, which part 1 (#30288) already made false; it now says a failed read behind a `team`, `position` or `queue` entry refuses the node, and keeps the literal statement for `department` and `org_membership_level`. No page in `skills/**` states what a queue answers on a failed read.

## What changes

Part 2 of #29604, under claim 6648819700 and seat ruling 6648946388, now that #30251 (PR #30318) put `onFailedRead` on the contract. Part 1 (PR #30288, `13c0c5baa`) is merged.

**1. `OwnershipQueueService` honours `onFailedRead` (`plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts`).**

- `expandMembers(name, org, { purpose?, onFailedRead? })` and `isMember(user, name, org, { onFailedRead? })` take the contract's option. The per-call `ExpansionPass` carries `refuse`, an axis of its own beside `purpose`.
- Under `'refuse'`, every read behind the queue passes its failure on instead of contributing nobody: the `sys_queue` row lookup (`authoredQueueRow`, which now words its own failure as `the sys_queue row of queue '<name>' in organization '<org>' could not be read: …`), the `sys_queue_member` walk (`authoredMemberSpecs`), each specification's expansion (`expandSpec`) and each team or position holder check (`holderCheck`). The paged reads already refuse on a failed page or an incomplete walk (part 1 / #29503), so a refusal is never an answer on the pages already read.
- The public call wraps the failure once, in `queueReadRefusal`: `[queue] queue '<name>' in organization '<org>' does not answer its members, because a read behind it failed: <the read, in its own words>. The caller asked for a refusal over a partial answer (onFailedRead 'refuse'): …`. The inner read loses its `[sharing]` tag and its own closing consequence ("…, so the expansion refuses instead."), and rides along whole as `cause`.
- `isMember` under `'refuse'` walks every specification: a later one that reaches the user still answers `true`, since a read that succeeded and found the user is a fact a failure beside it cannot remove. Only when none reaches does the first failure become the answer. So `false` is answered only when every read succeeded, as the contract says. The queue's own `sys_queue` / `sys_queue_member` reads come first and reject before any specification is read, because without them the call does not know what to ask.
- Under `'nobody'`, the default, nothing moves: each failed read contributes nobody, logged once. `resolveQueue`, `queuesOf`, `queuesNaming` and `hasAnyQueue` take no option and keep that answer.
- The activation-ledger read (`switchedOff`) keeps reading "switched on" when it fails, under both answers. The contract left that to this card; see Acceptance notes.
- The module header and the `holderCheck` / `readFailureReason` comments no longer say the refusal waits on the contract.

**2. D7, the sharing-recipient grant recompute (`plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts`).** The `queue` branch of `expandRecipient` and of `ruleReachesUser` pass `{ onFailedRead: 'refuse' }`. `expandRecipient` feeds the whole-rule pass (`desiredGrantsForRule`), the recipient-axis revoke (`revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients`, which expands before it diffs) and the record pass (`expandRecipientForRecord`); `ruleReachesUser` feeds the per-user pass (`reconcileRuleForUser`). In each, the refusal throws before any grant is diffed or revoked, so the rule's grants stay as they were. No new catch was needed: each production caller already isolates a refusing rule and warns, as it has for `team` and `position` recipients since #29503 / #29362 (`evaluateAllForRecord`, `evaluateAllRulesForObject`, the queue-hooks and BU-tree recomputes, the membership-row recompute, the boot backfill).

**3. D6, the approver slate (`plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`).** `expandQueueUsers` passes `{ purpose: 'addressing', onFailedRead: 'refuse' }`. Part 1's catch in `resolveApproverSpec` already turns a `queue` expansion's rejection into `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` before the "expanded to nobody" return, so a queue the registered service cannot read now refuses the node under every `onEmptyApprovers` policy, the fallback slate included, with the queue's failed read as `failedRead`.

**4. Admission consumers untouched.** The sitting-record access path (`SharingService` → `isMember` / `queuesOf`), the claim gate (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` → `isMember`), `explain-access`, and the assignment pool (`objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts` → `expandMembers`) call without the option and answer nobody on a failed read, as before.

**5. Changeset.** The new `29604-queue-service-refuses-failed-read.md` (BREAKING, `!`, Clause-② narrowing, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) carries this part. Its last bullet honours part 1's "Not yet": it names the two sentences of part 1's pending entry (its `Clause-②:` sentence that the service "does not reject yet", and its **Not yet** bullet) and says they no longer hold and are to be read as this bullet. Part 1's file itself is left as it stands on `main`; see Acceptance notes.

## Tests

All new pins sit in the existing shared harnesses as top-level `describe`s. Each `⛔` case was run against `origin/main`'s three source files with this branch's tests: every one is red there.

- `ownership-queue.test.ts`, "onFailedRead 'refuse' rejects a failed read, naming it (#29604)", 7 cases on the shared fake engine (one table's reads made to throw):
  - a failed `sys_queue` read rejects `expandMembers` and `isMember`, naming the row read, with no warning; the default still answers `[]` / `false`, warned once;
  - a failed `sys_queue_member` read rejects, never the declared positions alone (default: the positions alone);
  - a failed `sys_team_member`, `sys_user_position` or `sys_member` read behind a specification rejects with the exact read sentence, without "refuses instead", and the driver error as `cause`;
  - `isMember` under refuse: `true` when a read that succeeded reaches the user, with the failing specification before or after it; a rejection for a user only the failed read could reach, and for a non-member; the default answers `false` for the same user;
  - facts stay facts: an empty queue `[]`, an unresolved name `[]` / `false`, healthy reads equal to the default;
  - a refusal is not remembered: the next call, once the table reads, answers the members;
  - a failed activation-ledger read is not a failed read under refuse either: "switched on", logged.
- `ownership-queue.test.ts`, D3 `describe`, 1 control: with `sys_team_member` failing, the access path gives a team-only member no access and throws nothing, and a position member keeps access.
- `queue-recipient.test.ts`, "a failed queue-member read keeps the queue-recipient rule's grants (#29604)", 5 cases through the real `OwnershipQueueService` and `SharingRuleService` over one engine (queue `billing` = user `u_c` + team `t_night` → `u_d`): the whole-rule pass rejects and revokes nothing, for a failed `sys_queue_member` and for a failed `sys_team_member`; the recipient-axis revoke rejects and retires nobody; the per-user pass rejects for `u_d` and still answers `u_c`; the record pass keeps the grants and warns per rule with the queue's refusal; once the read succeeds, the next pass converges (a member who left loses the grant). The existing case "grants each member the expander returns" now pins the third argument `{ onFailedRead: 'refuse' }`. The fake engine gained a `failing` set.
- `approval-service.test.ts`, "a queue approver asks the queue service to refuse a failed read, and the node refuses with it (ADR-0142 D6)", 4 cases, one per `onEmptyApprovers` policy: a queue double that answers as the registered service does (rejects under `'refuse'`, `[]` under `'nobody'`) is asked `{ purpose: 'addressing', onFailedRead: 'refuse' }`, and the node refuses with `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` whose `failedRead` is the queue's refusal, logs no "expanded to nobody" and writes no request, approver or action row. The existing "asked for ADDRESSING" case pins the new option too.

## Acceptance notes

- **Activation ledger, decided: no move.** The contract says whether its failure posture moves is this card's to decide. It stays "switched on" under both answers: it is the posture the sharing-rule service takes for the same ledger on its own `position` recipients (`positionConfersAccess`), so a queue's position and a rule's position cannot disagree during the outage, and the D6 slate reads positions on the addressing purpose, which skips the position ledger. The cost, stated: during such an outage a D7 pass can grant the holders of a position that is switched off. That predates this card and is unchanged here.
- **`isMember` under refuse answers `true` when a successful read reaches the user.** The contract fixes when `false` may be answered ("only when every read behind it succeeded"); it does not say a failure beside a positive read refuses. Refusing there would make the answer depend on specification order, and on D7 it would hold back a grant the user is owed.
- **The queue's own rows refuse first.** A failed `sys_queue` or `sys_queue_member` read rejects `isMember` even for a declared queue whose positions might reach the user, since the call cannot know the queue's full membership without them.
- **Follow-up owed, spec wording (no spec file changed here, as dispatched):** in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts`, `OwnershipQueueFailedReadAnswer`: (1) "the registered one … honours `'refuse'` from #29604's code half on, so until then a caller passing `'refuse'` still gets `'nobody'`" can drop its "until then"; (2) "whether that posture moves is #29604's code half to decide" can state the decision (it does not move); (3) `isMember`'s doc could say that `true` is answered when a read that succeeded reaches the user, even beside a failed one.
- **Part 1's pending changeset is not edited here; a person decides whether it is.** Two of its sentences (the `Clause-②:` line's "The registered ownership-queue service does not reject yet: …" and the **Not yet** bullet) become false when this merges, while both entries are still unreleased. I first corrected them in place, and `check-empty-changeset` refused it as designed: rewriting a pending note on the merge base is a release decision that needs a person's confirmation, and the gate stays red until then. So this PR leaves the file as on `main` and supersedes the two sentences from its own entry instead. If the maintainer prefers the note corrected in place, it is a three-line change (`.changeset/29604-approver-directory-refusal-queue-paging.md`) that I can push once confirmed, with that gate red by design.
- **Docs correction rides along.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` had kept part 1's stale sentence (a `team` / `position` entry whose holder read failed keeps its literal). Part 1's PR body said no page stated it; that was wrong, and this PR fixes the page.
- **Assignee and reviewers:** none set, as dispatched.
